*sigh* Let me sit down and think about this year. My back's been bothering me but the wheat doesn't wait for nobody.

---

## My thinking, in my own words

I've been working this land for thirty-five years. My husband does some hauling work in town when there's no harvest, so most days it's just me out there with the hoe. Ten mu and a bit isn't much, but for two old people it's plenty when the back hurts.

**About my fields.** I keep the wheat-maize on the better piece, about six mu, the part with the smoother soil close to the well. The other four mu I keep in cotton because that's how my mother-in-law did it and that ground has always been cotton ground. Some neighbors have stopped growing cotton because of all the work, but I still do it — it brings in cash in the autumn and we need that.

**Wheat that's already in the ground.** I planted the wheat back in October like always, the seed I bought from the same shop in town — they call it "good wheat for our area," I don't remember the name. About one bag per mu of the 15-15-15 compound when I plowed and planted, that's how it's always been. Now the wheat is greening up. In a few weeks I'll spread some urea, maybe a bit more than half a bag per mu, when I do the spring watering. Urea has gotten so dear — last year a bag was eighty-something yuan, this year they want over a hundred. I'll do what I can. If the wheat looks pale at jointing I'll add a little more, if it looks dark green I'll save the money.

**Watering.** I'll water two or three times — once when it greens up, once at jointing, and one more before the grain fills if it's dry. The well water costs money to pump and the meter ticks fast. Last year I only watered twice because of the drought permit thing and the wheat still gave me about four hundred catties per mu, not bad.

**About the maize.** Soon as the combine cuts the wheat in early June I have to get the maize in fast — five days, maybe a week, no more. I hire a man with the seeder, he comes through the village and does it for thirty yuan per mu. I put a bit of compound under and then urea once more when the maize is knee-high. Maize doesn't need as much watering, the summer rains usually come.

**About the cotton.** Plant late April when the soil warms up. I'll lay the plastic mulch like always — I buy a roll from town. Cotton is the hard one. So much spraying, so much picking. My niece comes from her village to help with the picking in autumn and I pay her, otherwise I couldn't do it. Cotton prices have been so-so for years now. I keep planting it because I know how, and the cash from selling in October helps with winter expenses.

**Money worries.** Fertilizer keeps going up, the diesel for the well keeps going up, the seed keeps going up. Cotton price doesn't keep up. I cut where I can — less spray when I don't see bugs, less water when it rained, no fancy seed.

**What I expect to harvest.** If it's a normal year — wheat about 400 catties per mu, maize about 450, cotton maybe 250 of lint. Good year a bit more, bad year a bit less. The Lord decides.
